tools.name: icp_deep_dive
tools.description: Analyze customer data to detect ICP patterns (industry, size, deal size, sales cycle, tech stack, triggers, champion roles). Ties are named as ties, the budget is the ACV range seen in your customers, and sector notes are added when your inputs name one of the supported sectors

customers.description: List of customer objects with available attributes

customer_descriptions.description: Alternative: Describe your best customers in text format

product_category.description: What type of product you sell

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out

tools.title: ICP Deep Dive

tools.name: icp_scoring_model
tools.description: Create a lead qualification scoring template: criteria with example point weights set by importance level, example points for each value you list, a scorecard and tier bands to adjust. Your success pattern is matched to your criteria; it does not set the weights. Sector notes are added when your inputs name one of the supported sectors Ask for held-back test counts and the pre-agreed stop rule when a model has been tested.

scoring_criteria.description: Criteria for scoring with importance levels

correlation_direction.description: Optional confirmed direction of the success pattern. Ask the user whether the named values correlate with better or worse outcomes before filling this. Overrides word reading; unknown withholds a top-points recommendation.

success_correlation.description: What correlates with success? (e.g., "deals with VP Sales champion close 2x faster")

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell, as a product category, so the scoring notes use your sector

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

held_back_test.description: Optional results on deals held back before tuning. Ask for the counts and the stop rule set before the test. A missed rule holds the scoring model; do not tune on this set.

tools.title: ICP Scoring Model

tools.name: buyer_group_analyzer
tools.description: Map the buyer group for a deal: the champion you name, your known stakeholders placed by their titles (economic buyer, technical evaluator, reviewers, users), each role's concern and message prompts, an influence map and discovery questions. Sector roles and questions are added when your inputs name one of the supported sectors

known_stakeholders.description: Roles you know are involved. A title suggests a role, not confirmed authority. Confirm who owns this purchase budget.

confirmed_budget_owner.description: Optional confirmed fact: the person or role who owns the budget for this purchase. Ask the user; do not infer from title. Overrides candidate ordering.

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out

tools.title: Buyer Group Analyzer

tools.name: tam_sam_som_calculator
tools.description: Use when someone says size my market, market sizing, or how big is my market. Before calling, ask what they sell, how many companies could buy and the annual contract value; never estimate these. Clarify what unlabelled numbers mean. Calculate TAM, SAM and SOM from supplied figures, not market research. Values are displayed in USD only; for rupees ask for a user-confirmed USD amount, never relabel or invent a conversion. Rates use 0 to 100 percentage points: ask whether 0.2 means 0.2% or a fraction meaning 20%. Omitted rates are labelled examples.

total_potential_companies.description: Number of companies that could buy, supplied by the user or a source they identify. Ask if missing; never estimate.

average_contract_value.description: Annual contract value in USD, confirmed by the user. This tool displays dollars only. Do not pass rupees as dollars or invent an exchange rate; ask for a confirmed USD amount.

icp_percentage.description: Percentage of potential companies that match the ideal customer profile, from 0 to 100. A value of 0.2 means 0.2%, not 20%. Clarify fraction notation first; convert an explicitly confirmed fraction to percentage points. Omitted: 30%, labelled as an example.

year1_market_share_target.description: Year 1 share as percentage points from 0 to 100. Clarify fractions: 0.03 means 0.03%, not 3%. Use only a confirmed value; omitted: 3%, labelled as an example.

data_sources.description: Where you got your numbers (for documentation)

product_category.description: Ask what they sell before calling. Use their words for the product or service; do not invent a category. Used for context, not arithmetic.

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

tools.title: TAM SAM SOM Calculator

tools.name: lookalike_signal_generator
tools.description: Generate platform-specific targeting criteria and search queries from your firmographics, technographics, champion titles and buying triggers (generates criteria, not data). Each trigger gets its own signal; search keywords come from what you sell and the sector; platforms limits the sections

platforms.description: Optional: the sections to include (linkedin, google_ads, 6sense, zoominfo). Left out, every section is included

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell (for example "spend management software"), used for search keywords and sector notes

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

tools.title: Lookalike Signal Generator

tools.name: account_prioritization
tools.description: Rank and prioritize accounts by a weighted score of fit, intent, relationship and timing; each account shows the points its timing earned and the factor that added the most points

intent_signals.description: 0 to 100 (0 scores zero). Left out, 50 is used

relationship.description: 0 to 100, based on existing connections. Left out, 50 is used

timing.description: Buying horizon: now, soon, later or unknown (100, 70, 40 and 50 points respectively). Equivalent phrases are read by clause; denied or conflicting horizons remain unknown. Confirm the horizon with the user.

accounts.description: List of accounts to prioritize. Each account: name, fit score (0 to 100), intent signals (0 to 100), relationship (0 to 100), timing (now, soon, later or unknown)

prioritization_weights.description: Optional custom weights in percent for fit, intent, relationship and timing. A missing weight uses its default (40, 30, 15, 15); the tool does not check that the weights sum to 100

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell (for example "spend management software"), used for sector notes. The arithmetic does not use it

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

tools.title: Account Prioritization

tools.name: icp_gap_analysis
tools.description: Analyze gaps between your current customer base and your ideal ICP: what the ideal profile has that the current base lacks, metric gaps from your current and target figures, causes to check and actions that fit your business model. Sector notes are added when your inputs name one of the supported sectors

current_customers.description: Description of your current customer base

ideal_icp.description: Description of your ideal customer profile

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell, used for sector notes

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out

tools.title: ICP Gap Analysis

tools.name: icp_evolution_tracker
tools.description: Review how your ICP should evolve: reads your recent wins, losses and market changes against your current ICP, states a candidate change for each (an addition to test, a disqualifier to test, an implication to check) and writes a draft of the updated ICP, with the roles your ICP does not name, the loss reasons to tag and what to pull from your CRM. It does not compute win rates; check each candidate against your CRM

time_period.description: Time period you are reviewing, in your own words (for example "last quarter")

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell, used for sector notes

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

tools.title: ICP Evolution Tracker

tools.name: icp_interview_synthesizer
tools.description: Extract ICP patterns from structured customer interview notes (customer, role, pain points, buying triggers, value realized and key quotes per interview): pain points, objections, buying triggers, value realized, champion roles and quotes kept word for word, with discovery questions and sector notes. It does not take full transcripts; give only the points and quotes you want analyzed.

interview_notes.description: Structured interview notes: one object per interview with the customer (company or segment), the role of the person interviewed and the points and quotes to analyze

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell, used for sector notes

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it

tools.title: ICP Interview Synthesizer
